1.explanation:
• docs/minimal.qmd – a bare-bones Quarto document showing default front matter and output formats used when you ‘quarto render’ (i.e. how the default LaTeX class and template are invoked).
• docs/bug-repros/issue-1340/index.qmd – an example of a minimal, self-contained bug repro with a single .qmd and a standard Quarto project layout.  Use this pattern to confirm the spacing issue.
• docs/crossrefs/theorems.qmd – shows how Quarto defines and numbers theorem blocks (definitions, examples, theorems, proofs) and how anchors/cross-refs are injected around them.
• docs/crossrefs/theorem-types.qmd – additional examples of custom theorem-type definitions and how Quarto’s LaTeX writer wraps those environments, so you can inspect where \leavevmode… is added.
• docs/crossrefs/sections.qmd – illustrates how Quarto handles headings and hypertarget anchors at the start of blocks; this is the same mechanism that is pre-pending code to definition/theorem blocks and is at the root of the extra vertical space.
1.bug_scenario:
In the LaTeX‐generated PDF output from Quarto (using the “scrreprt” class), every definition, theorem or example block is being pushed down by an extra vertical gap.  If you inspect the .tex it’s because Quarto is injecting an anchor macro

    \leavevmode\vadjust pre{\hypertarget{…}{}}%

immediately before the \begin{definition}/\begin{theorem}/etc.  That one extra line of code creates unwanted space above each block.  In addition, proofs rendered by Quarto end with a blank line before \end{proof}, which causes the QED symbol to sit lower than in handwritten LaTeX, where there is no empty line.

The two screenshots show (1) the Quarto‐rendered PDF with large gaps and a low QED symbol and (2) a hand-written .tex version, without the injected \leavevmode… code and without the final blank line, giving a tight block and a correctly placed QED.
